subject: Data segregation and learning-prohibition request for PulseCloud pilot
messages:
From: Matthew Liu <matthew.liu@pulsecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Segregated capture + no-adaptive-learning for pilot (PulseCloud)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Legal at PulseCloud has a couple of gating questions before procurement signs off on the pilot. High level: we need a contractual commitment that interactions captured from our tenant will not be used to improve general models (no adaptive training) and that our captured data will be stored in a segregated lane (onshore residency preferred).

Specifically can you confirm the following and share any operational artifacts you can provide:
- A proposed no-adaptive-training clause we can include in the DPA
- How Redwood segregates tenant captures at rest (S3 bucket per tenant? prefixes?) and whether we can have a dedicated export path (SFTP or customer-managed bucket)
- Proof of controls: a sample audit log extract or description of the audit trail for token access; list of subprocessors and their regions
- Whether outputs generated by the model are considered tenant-owned (we prefer tenant-owned outputs and an explicit non-derivative commitment)

PulseCloud legal attached a draft DPA for reference (will send separately).

Can we get a brief ops/legal write-up this week so procurement can review?

Appreciate it —
Matt
Matthew Liu
Head of Integrations, PulseCloud

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Liu <matthew.liu@pulsecloud.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segregated capture + no-adaptive-learning for pilot (PulseCloud)

Hi Matt —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can commit to a contract-backed no-adaptive-training restriction for the tenant interactions captured during your pilot, and we can operate a segregated capture path with onshore residency options. I've attached a short ops/legal outline that summarizes the commitment and the operational controls (redwood_no_train_ops_outline.pdf). Highlights below for procurement and your legal team: 

1) No-adaptive-training clause (suggested language):
"Redwood will not use PulseCloud tenant interactions or derived artifacts to improve or adapt any models or model weights outside the isolated environment serving PulseCloud, except as required for security or compliance investigations, and only with prior written consent."

2) Segregated capture model:
- Default: tenant-dedicated object prefix within a region-specific bucket with access controls and customer-dedicated encryption keys (KMS).
- Upgrade option: dedicated S3 bucket or dedicated tenant capacity (reserved instance) for environments requiring physical isolation.

3) Export & custody:
- We support scheduled SFTP exports and one-click customer-managed exports to an S3 bucket you control (we provide presigned URLs / transfer helpers).

4) Proof & evidence we can provide up-front:
- Sample audit log extract showing object creation, read access, and key-rotation events
- Current subprocessor list with geographies (we can whiteboard which subprocessors will touch captured artifacts for the pilot)
- Snapshot of our no-adaptive-training gating: a config flag at the tenant scope that prevents routing of tenant captures to any model-improvement pipelines; change to this flag requires multi-person ops approval and documented change log.

5) Outputs and derivative rights:
- Our standard approach for pilots is to grant tenant ownership over outputs and provide a non-derivative commitment for customer-specific datasets. We can include a clause in the DPA specifying tenant ownership of generated outputs and an explicit non-derivative license to Redwood only for debugging and support (time-limited and redacted).

Next steps I propose:
- David (ops) and Kimberly (legal) are cc'd to confirm operational feasibility and to provide the sample artifacts.
- We'll prepare a short appendix that you can attach to your DPA and mark it as evidence of operational controls.

If that sounds good I can have the appendix + the sample logs and subprocessor list to you by EOD Monday.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_no_train_ops_outline.pdf (pdf)
